title: Ὁδοιπόρος καὶ Τύχη
source: Émile Chambry, Ésope: Fables, texte établi et traduit (Les Belles Lettres, Paris, 1927), fable 261. Text as printed, including Chambry's editorial punctuation (« »). Pronunciation: reconstructed Attic, after W. S. Allen, Vox Graeca. Romanization: standard classical transliteration (ē/ō; th/ph/ch; y for υ, u in diphthongs; h = rough breathing; ēi/āi/ōi for iota subscript; accents omitted).

sentences.t: Ὁδοιπόρος πολλὴν ὁδὸν διανύσας, ἐπειδὴ κόπῳ συνείχετο, πεσὼν παρά τι φρέαρ ἐκοιμᾶτο.
sentences.tr: Hodoiporos pollēn hodon dianysas, epeidē kopōi syneicheto, pesōn para ti phrear ekoimato.
sentences.l: A traveller, having completed a long road, since he was held fast by weariness, having fallen down beside a well, was sleeping.
sentences.i: A traveller who had gone a long way, gripped by weariness, dropped down beside a well and fell asleep.
sentences.n: συνέχομαι is to be held together and so held fast, with κόπῳ the dative of what holds him. φρέαρ is a dug well, open at the top — which is what makes the next line dangerous.

sentences.t: Μέλλοντος δὲ αὐτοῦ ὅσον οὔπω καταπίπτειν, ἡ Τύχη ἐπιστᾶσα καὶ διεγείρασα αὐτὸν εἶπεν· « Ὦ οὗτος, εἴγε ἐπεπτώκεις, οὐκ ἂν τὴν σεαυτοῦ ἀβουλίαν, ἀλλ’ ἐμὲ ᾐτιῶ. »
sentences.tr: Mellontos de autou hoson oupō katapiptein, hē Tychē epistasa kai diegeirasa auton eipen· « Ō houtos, eige epeptōkeis, ouk an tēn seautou aboulian, all’ eme ēitiō. »
sentences.l: And he being on the point of falling in at any moment, Fortune, having stood over him and having roused him, said: « You there, if indeed you had fallen in, you would have blamed not your own want of counsel, but me. »
sentences.i: And just as he was on the point of falling in, Fortune stood over him, woke him and said: « You there — had you fallen in, you would have laid the blame not on your own thoughtlessness but on me. »
sentences.n: A genitive absolute opens the sentence, and ὅσον οὔπω, 'as much as not yet', is the idiom for the very edge of a thing — all but already. ἐπιστᾶσα, 'having stood over', is the regular verb for a god or a dream taking its place beside a sleeper. The condition is contrary to fact in past time: εἴγε with the pluperfect ἐπεπτώκεις, and ἄν with the imperfect ᾐτιῶ.

sentences.t: Οὕτω πολλοὶ τῶν ἀνθρώπων δι’ ἑαυτοὺς δυστυχήσαντες τοὺς θεοὺς αἰτιῶνται.
sentences.tr: Houtō polloi tōn anthrōpōn di’ heautous dystychēsantes tous theous aitiōntai.
sentences.l: Thus many among men, having fared badly through themselves, blame the gods.
sentences.n: Almost the same close as fable 131. δι’ ἑαυτούς, 'because of themselves', puts the cause exactly where Fortune has just put it.
